name: THE VOLUME-AT-A-TIME SWEEP OF 1988-1993, AND WHAT IT SETTLES
kind: method that worked, and a definitive negative
fact: Every leaf of six Talismans was rendered from the embedded scan and OCR'd with ocrmac at twice native size, and the whole worklist was then matched against the result in one pass instead of person by person: 1988 (389 leaves), 1989 (189), 1990 (375), 1991 (190), 1992 (185) and 1993 (144), 1,472 leaves and 127,157 lines of text. Cost about forty minutes of machine time with four sweeps running at once, roughly 1.2 seconds a page. IT WORKS AND IT SHOULD BE THE DEFAULT. It found in one pass what eight person-by-person passes had missed, and it produces a negative that can be trusted. THE THREE THINGS IT TURNED UP THAT THE INDEX ROUTE COULD NOT. First, the 1988 volume had never been swept by this block at all. It covers 1987-88, the year BEFORE the earliest cohort here, which is exactly where the 1988-89 intake sit as freshmen and sophomores, and it is where Elaine Burge's portrait was, in the freshman grid on p. 347. Always work the volume before the first year of service, not only the years of service and after. Second, the portrait grids are keyed to margin name blocks that the back index does not always index, so a person absent from an index can still be in a grid, and the reverse. Third, an organisation photograph with a positional caption is a portrait source, not just a name list, and the write-off entry in _archive-gaps.json about thirty-one members of 1990-91 to 1994-95 is wrong on that point: it reasons that a person 'named in an index but only on organization or story pages ... never sat for a portrait', which is true of the grids and does not mean there is no usable face. Ginger Markham was written off that way and her face is on 1993 p. 202. WHAT THE SWEEP PROVES NEGATIVELY: the following people are in NO portrait grid of any of the six volumes, checked line by line at the exact alphabetical position with fuzzy matching for OCR damage, and in most cases are absent from the volumes entirely. For several the volumes hold a near neighbour that will tempt a later pass and is a different person: Sherry and Nicole Gaddis but no Chris; Dana, Rebekah, Clarence and Emily Shirley and a Shirley Green but no Johnna; Ann Michele Dillard but no Dawn; Anne, Lori Ann, James T. and Lisa Duncan and a Duncan Gibson but no Derrek and no Jeff; Amy, Kelley, Vikki, Jeffery, Willie, Reece, Donald, Charles, James, Melissa, Juliane and Tricia Carter but no Margaret; Sherry Woods, Karen Wood, Donna Wood and JoAnn Woodruff but no Jo Wood; Devon and Laura Pinkston but no Shawn; Loretta Welch but no Kendra; Jeff Schreiner but no Molly; Justin Carlisle but no Jeff; Stacey Brawner but no Darron; Sondra Jeffries but no Susanne. name: THE 1986 AND 1987 TALISMANS ON ARCHIVE.ORG ARE THE BEST SOURCE THIS BLOCK HAS
kind: source found, and it is four times the resolution of anything else here
fact: archive.org holds the Talisman for 1943-1981, 1986 and 1987 and NOTHING between 1988 and 1993, checked against its advanced-search API on 4 September 2026: talisman1988west through talisman1993west all return empty metadata. So the note in _archive-gaps.json that says to prefer archive.org copies over TopSCHOLAR for 1982-1991 cannot be followed for the volumes that cover this block's own years; those must come off TopSCHOLAR at about 96 dpi. But 1986 and 1987 CAN, and they scan at 3282 by 4500 pixels a page against TopSCHOLAR's 880, which is nearly four times the linear resolution. THAT CHANGES WHAT COUNTS AS A USABLE GROUP PHOTOGRAPH. A face in a fifteen-person club picture, worth 30 pixels on a TopSCHOLAR page and therefore worthless, comes out 200 pixels here. Three of this run's finds are from the 1987 volume and all three are far better than anything cut from 1988-1993: Becky Shirley's sophomore portrait at 360 by 435, Lisa Kaufman at 187 by 250 out of a thirteen-woman Alpha Delta Pi group, Joe Leffert at 205 by 295 out of a fifteen-person University Scholars group. Use scripts/talisman.py, which searches the OCR text stream and maps a hit back to a leaf; search the surname alone, and treat the leaf it returns as a pointer only, because the text stream pools captions from several leaves away. The reliable route is the back index: search 'Surname,' to get the index line, which gives printed page numbers, then pull leaf = page + 3. WHO THIS SEAM IS FOR: anyone whose first SGA year is 1988-89 or 1989-90 was at Western in 1986-87, and the whole 1988-89 cohort of this block was run against both volumes on this pass. Blocks whose people served 1985-86 to 1987-88 should work these two volumes before anything else.

One name against one face, no counting, no row-and-column reasoning, no sex test - the strongest identification this archive accepts, and it is on a board scanned at 4209 by 3474, so a single portrait crops out at about 370 by 400 with no upscaling. The existing notes on Spirit Masters in _archive-gaps.json are all about the 2011-2018 BOOKLETS, which are closed, and about the scrapboards pairing by column, which is fragile. This is a different thing: a labelled composite. Nine scrapbooks exist at stu_org/321-329 and their record pages give the year each covers - 321 is 1989-90, 322 is 1994-95, 323 is 2001-02, 324 is 1985-86, 326 is 2011-12, 327 is 2004-05, 328 is 2007-08, 329 is 1996-97. The Opinion page sets a letter signature in the same bold-name-over-italic-town-and-class as the People Poll, which is why a geometry sweep finds them and why six false hits were reported on an earlier run. Nothing of Alex Rose is photographed in 1993-2005.

name: Alex Rose
kind: photographed twice, both refused - no usable face
fact: He is the only person of the whole 1992-97 target list who is photographed in BOTH digitised volumes, and neither picture yields a face. 1993 Talisman p. 109, indexed "Rose, Alex 109": a full-page photograph shot from high above a racquetball court, captioned "Nashville junior Alex Rose warms up on the racquetball court while waiting for his opponent to arrive" (credit Joe Carwile). One figure, correctly identified by the caption, but taken from directly overhead and from behind - the top of his head and his back, no face at all. 1994 Talisman p. 23, indexed "Rose, Alex, 23": captioned "Nashville senior Alex Rose checks out his dental work in the mirror of a makeover artist who visited Schneider Hall lobby. Dormmates Louisville senior Glen Siegel and Gamaliel senior Jeff Murray watch in amusement." Three men are in the frame. The grammar does place Rose: he is the one holding and looking into the mirror, back to the camera, while the other two named men are the watchers. But his face appears only as a reflection in the small mirror, mouth stretched wide open over his teeth, about 50 by 58 pixels at native scan resolution. No reader could recognise a person from it. NOTE FOR A LATER PASS: the Herald corroborates the Talisman's Alex Rose exactly - "Alex Rose, Nashville junior" signing a letter on 4 Mar 1993 and "Alex Rose, Nashville senior" on 4 Nov 1993 and 22 Feb 1994 - and by autumn 1994 he was a Herald guest columnist controversial enough to be debated in Garrett. The Herald never ties him to SGA, and there is a separate Ashley Rose who was SGA Executive Secretary in 1993 and a separate Kibby Rose in the 1993 ASG group photograph, so do not assume the columnist and the Representative at Large are one man without a source. If a photograph of the columnist turns up in the Herald it will still need that link.

name: ABSENT FROM BOTH DIGITISED TALISMAN GRIDS - 20 people of the n8892 block, sweep of 7 September 2026
kind: written off: swept both volumes whole, checked at the exact alphabetical position
fact: METHOD, and it is the volume-at-a-time grid sweep, not an index lookup name by name. Both digitised volumes were opened whole and every printed page read: 1993 Talisman (dlsc_ua_records/417, 144 leaves) and 1994 Talisman (dlsc_ua_records/418, 148 leaves). 84 portrait grid pages were identified from the page images and 1,982 name labels were parsed off them with their cell positions - 1,047 in the 1993 volume and 935 in the 1994. THE GRID PAGES ARE: 1993 pp. 20-21 graduates, 24-46 seniors, 48-54 juniors, 56-62 sophomores, 63-74 freshmen, 76-80 faculty and staff, with the TOP OF THE HILL feature pages interleaved at 25, 31, 35, 39, 47, 51, 55, 59, 67, 71 and 75 and carrying no portraits; 1994 pp. 22-47 by residence hall then Off-Campus, 57-70 by greek chapter, 79-80 faculty and staff. LAYOUT, verified against the page images rather than assumed. 1993: four portraits across, five rows deep, the twenty names set in ONE COLUMN down the LEFT margin in blocks of four against each grid row, alphabetical left to right - read off p. 78, whose second block is Anna Jo Johnson, Horace Johnson Jr., Cynthia Y. Jones, Kaveh Khatir against four faces F M F M. 1994: five across, six deep, the thirty names in ONE COLUMN down the RIGHT margin in blocks of five, alphabetical left to right - read off p. 59 and p. 63, where the alphabet runs unbroken down three blocks and then restarts at a fresh chapter heading. THE BACK INDEXES were then re-OCR'd column by column at 5x, because the pooled page OCR reads these four-column pages badly: the 1993 index had a hole running from Seebold straight to Templeton, losing the whole Sh-Sm-St-Ta run including every Smith. That gives 1,739 complete index entries for 1993 and 1,240 for 1994, with no gap anywhere in the alphabet. Every target was then matched in one pass against the grid labels, against the indexes, and against all 16,432 raw OCR items of both volumes, with one-edit tolerance on surnames and nickname expansion on first names. WHY THE ANSWER IS THIS THIN, and it is not a failure of the sweep. Two things. FIRST, neither book photographs the whole student body. The 1993 volume's People section is a paid-sitting selection - about 1,047 portraits including faculty - and the 1994 volume's is organised by residence hall and greek chapter and comes to about 935. Against a student body of some 15,000 that is roughly one student in fifteen, so the base rate of any given senator appearing is about 7 per cent whatever else is true. SECOND, and this is the bigger one: THE 1994 TALISMAN IS THE LAST BOOK WITH PORTRAIT GRIDS AND IT COVERS 1993-94. There is no 1995 volume - record 419 and its neighbours are the Xposure magazines, which carry no grids - and nothing after that until 2013. So a person whose first recorded SGA year is 1995-96 or 1996-97 was, in the year the last grid book went to press, either not yet at Western or a first-year who had not sat. Of the 134 people on this sweep's target list, 87 have a first year of 1995-96 or 1996-97, and not one of those 87 appears anywhere in either volume - not in a grid, not in a group photograph, not in an index line. That is the structural answer to the 1990s block and it should stop anyone sending another agent at these two books for the 1995-97 cohort. RESULT FOR THIS BLOCK: of the 20 people listed here, NOT ONE appears in a portrait grid, in a group photograph, in a caption or in either back index. Each was checked at its exact alphabetical position in both indexes and the immediate neighbours on either side are recorded in the 'checked' field below, so this can be audited without reopening the volumes. OFFICERS among them (3): Margaret Carter, Dawn Dillard, Derrek Duncan. RANK AND FILE (17): Jeff Carlisle, Jeff Duncan, Jill Howard, Susanne Jeffiers, Thomas Lally, Jim Lee, Trent Lyda, Kim Mann, Paula Miller, Laura Nunn, Von Parrish, Shawn Pinkston, Jill Reading, Molly Schreiner, Jenny Stelmach, Tim Sturm, Kendra Welch. WHAT DID TURN UP, all of it recorded in its own note or entry: Horace Johnson (1993 p. 78, but he is WKU's Public Safety Director and not an SGA officer at all), Edward Myers and Cinnamon Roberts (1993 p. 204, the ASG group photograph, printed row key, faces about 15 to 18 pixels and unusable), Alex Rose (1993 p. 109 shot from directly overhead, 1994 p. 23 a face only in a hand mirror), Nicki Jerome as Nicki Gerome (1994 p. 63, cut and flagged FACE PROVED PERSON NOT PROVED) and Crystal Smith (1994 p. 59, cut and flagged the same way). Six people out of 134, two crops, and both of those flagged. NEAR MISSES THAT WILL TEMPT A LATER PASS AND ARE DIFFERENT PEOPLE: 'John Taylor' at 1994 p. 202 is a Balltown freshman selling raffle tickets with his brother Phil, which cannot be the archive's Non-Traditional Representative of 1994-95; 'Tarvin, Brandon' is not Parvin; 'Cross Country' is not Criss; 'Smith' is not Stith; 'Eric Parsons' is not Yeric.

name: Margaret Carter
kind: candidate found and cut: WKU Nursing Class 1997 composite
fact: The WKU Department of Nursing Bachelor of Science Class of 1997 composite (WKU Archives UA61/1, TopSCHOLAR dlsc_ua_records/2530) carries a portrait with the printed nameplate PEGGY C. CARTER, fifth in the top row, alphabetically between Dana R. Carpenter and Patricia A. Chaisson RN. The face on that plate is proved by its own nameplate. IT IS NOT MARGARET CARTER AND WAS NOT CUT. THREE REASONS. FIRST, the Herald names her Margaret every time and never Peggy: 'freshman Margaret Carter' in the SGA election coverage of 15 April 1993, 'Lexington freshman Margaret Carter' on 20 and 22 April 1993 running for sophomore vice president against William Zorn, 'Lexington sophomore Margaret Carter' on 2 November 1995, and 'Lexington sophomore Margaret Carter' again on 29 February 1996 in the report of the Simpson Dilemma programme on conflict between black and white women, which is the same subject as the forum SGA's minutes have her working on as Cultural Diversity Committee chair on 5 March 1996. Equating Peggy with Margaret is a second inference stacked on the first, and the archive's own rule refuses that. SECOND, the years do not work. The Herald still calls her a SOPHOMORE in February 1996. A Bachelor of Science nursing class of 1997 is an upper-division clinical cohort, and a sophomore of spring 1996 is not in it. THIRD, Carter is a common surname on this campus: the archive already holds Don Carter, Juli Carter, Michaela Carter and Eli Carter. Nothing anywhere puts Margaret Carter in nursing. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND USEFUL: she was from LEXINGTON, she was a freshman in spring 1993 and a sophomore through spring 1996, and she ran for sophomore vice president in April 1993 against William Zorn. That is a better description of her than the archive previously held and it should make the next portrait search easier. NOTE ON THE SCAN: the Wayback copy of article 3533 is capped at exactly 1,048,576 bytes and the embedded 1743 by 1416 plate image decodes only about the top 55 per cent of its rows. The top three bands, which is where Carter sits, are legible; the lower bands are not. If anyone needs the bottom of this plate they will have to find another route to the file.

name: David Smith
kind: candidate found on a WKU class composite and cut
fact: UA61/1 WKU Nursing Class 1991 (dlsc_ua_records/2519) carries a portrait nameplated David Smith, and the plate year sits exactly on his first recorded SGA year. It was NOT cut. David Smith is the commonest name in the archive and in the country; the same 1991-92 minutes that name him also name a Donald Smith four places away on the same absence roll, which is the archive's own warning about Smiths in this Congress. Nothing states his major. He was also matched against UA61/1 WKU Nursing Class 1976 (dlsc_ua_records/2494), which is fifteen years too early and cannot be him. Without a source putting him in nursing this is not an identification and should not be revisited without one. CONTEXT: this came out of a sweep of every WKU class composite on TopSCHOLAR, 150 records and 4,429 roster names, run against all 796 people in the nine block worklists on 7 September 2026. The composites are UA60/5 dental hygiene 1972-2015 and UA61/1 nursing 1966-2011, plus the UA12/2/16 Spirit Masters class booklets 2011-2018, the UA61/16 physical therapy Class of 2016 and the UA60/5/1 dental hygiene scrapbooks.
